utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. For this afternoon, the testimony of Mr. Kabashi has been scheduled through videolink; however, we could not start with that at this time. Therefore, the Chamber would like to deal with a few procedural matters, deliver a few decisions, and then we'll hear whether the witness arrived at the location of the videolink. utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I would prefer to put in a considered reply, and I can organise that by writing by tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: By tomorrow. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I take the same position. Whether or not I will be filing a -- an independent reply or joining that which is being prepared by my colleague, I'll determine later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Troop.

utterances.speaker: MR. TROOP
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. We would like to take the same position, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber accepts the suggestion by Defence counsel, that is, that the Chamber would like to have responses filed by tomorrow close of business. Then the next issue I have on my list is an oral decision on the admission into evidence of Roel Versonnen's 92 ter statement and photo-board P1230. The Chamber delivers this decision where it has not yet decided on lifting the protective measures in relation to Witness 1, but since they are still in place, this has some consequences for the way in which this decision is delivered. The Chamber will now give its decision on the admission of P1225 and P1230. On the 12th and the 15th of November, the Chamber heard the evidence of the witness Roel Versonnen. The Prosecution tendered through this witness P1225, which is Mr. Versonnen's 92 ter statement. On the 12th of November, the Defence for Mr. Balaj objected to paragraphs 11, 15, 17, 19 and 20 of P1225; and the Defence for Mr. Haradinaj objected to a large part of paragraph 18. On the 15th of November, 2007, the Chamber decided that the information contained in paragraphs 14 through 19 was to be elicited viva voce. The Defence for Mr. Balaj dropped its objection to paragraph 11 but continued to object to paragraph 20. No objections were raised to paragraphs 1 through 13, and 21 and 22. The Chamber informed the parties that it would decide on admission at a later date. The Chamber considers paragraphs 1 through 13 and paragraphs 20 through 22 to be relevant and of probative value. The Chamber orders the Prosecution to redact all of paragraphs 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, and 19, upload the redacted statement into e-court, and inform the Registrar when this has been done. The Chamber orders the Registrar to replace the current content of P1225 while maintaining the same exhibit number. The Chamber admits the redacted statement into evidence under seal. P1225 mentions a witness who has been granted protective measures in the Haradinaj et al. case. The Chamber orders the Prosecution to redact -- to redact the statement so as to -- not to disclose the identity of Witness 1. So that's apart from the redaction I just ordered already, that is, redaction of paragraphs 14 through 19. The Chamber orders the Prosecution to upload this now doubly redacted version into e-court and inform the Registrar when this has been done. The Chamber instructs the Registrar to assign an exhibit number to it and inform the Chamber and parties of the exhibit number so assigned. The Chamber admits this doubly redacted statement into evidence. And that's, of course, the public version. P1230 is a photo-board used by the Prosecution during the examination-in-chief of witness Roel Versonnen. There have been no objections to the admission into evidence of P1230, and the Chamber admits P1230 into evidence. And this concludes the Chamber's ruling on this matter. The Chamber now delivers an oral decision, at this moment without reasons. It is an oral decision whether the testimony of Witness 56 was validly given. The decision of the Chamber is that the testimony was validly given. The reasons will follow in writing. Then I'd like to move into private session. No, let me just...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. The Chamber would now deliver its decision on the admission of two Rule 92 bis statements and the application for protective measures for Witnesses 68 and 42 in the tentative order of testimony. On the 15th of November, 2007, the Prosecution filed the above-mentioned requests, including to admit the statements dated the 13th and 14th of November, 2007 into evidence pursuant to Rule 92 bis, to assign the witnesses pseudonyms, and to keep their identities confidential. The Defence for Mr. Haradinaj, Mr. Balaj, and Mr. Brahimaj indicated informally on the 19th of November, 2007 that they agree to the tendering of the statements of the two witnesses provided that the word "kidnapped" in paragraph 7 of the statement of the 14th of November, 2007 be redacted. The Defence teams have further indicated that they do not oppose the application for protective measures for these witnesses. The statement of Witness 68 in the tentative order of testimony describes the disappearance of Nenad Remistar and what the witness had heard about this person's whereabouts from other persons after the disappearance. Witness 42 in the tentative order of testimony describes in her statement the disappearance of Rade Popadic when he was driving from Babaloc to Junik with his colleague. The statements are relevant to counts 29 and 30 and counts 21 and 22 of the indictment, respectively. They have probative value and do not contain information about the acts and conduct of the accused. Furthermore, the parties have agreed to the admission of the witnesses' statements, under the condition mentioned before. The Chamber therefore admits the statements dated the 13th and 14th of November, 2007 into evidence and orders the Prosecution to redact, I quote, "when he was kidnapped," in paragraph 7 of the statement of the 14th of November, 2007. The Prosecution shall upload the newly redacted version of the statement into e-court and inform the Registrar when it has done so. The Chamber instructs the Registrar to assign exhibit numbers to the two statements and inform the parties of the exhibit numbers so assigned. As for the application for protective measures, the legal test for granting such measures applied by this Chamber has been set forth numerous times, and there is no need to repeat it again. The testimony of Witness 68 in the tentative order of testimony may antagonise persons living in Kosovo, as the witness mentions in her statement that she received information that Nenad Remistar was held in KLA custody. Witness 68's family owns two houses and land in Kosovo and would like to return there to live. The parties have agreed that there is an unstable security situation in Kosovo which is particularly unfavourable to witnesses who appear before the Tribunal. The family of Witness 42 in the tentative order of testimony received repetitively threatening phone calls from Albanian-speaking persons between 2001 and 2006, the latest calls in April 2006, just before the witness was supposed to give a statement to the Prosecution. This means that the first part of the test is met. The Chamber further grants Witness 68 and Witness 42 protective measures of a pseudonym. It instructs the Registrar to assign pseudonym numbers to Witness 68 and Witness 42 in the tentative order of testimony and further orders that the un-redacted statements are admitted under seal and the redacted statements are admitted publicly. And this concludes the Chamber's decision. I will now move to admission of exhibits introduced through Witness 69. The redacted 92 ter statement of Witness 69, that is, 65 ter number 1720, should be assigned an exhibit number. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be P1231.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber has decided that P1231 is admitted into evidence. The Chamber is still considering whether or not to admit all or some of the attachments. If attachments would not be admitted, then the Chamber, of course, will consider what should be the consequences for those portions of P1231 in which the witness refers to the attachments. Of course, the Chamber will have to consider what remains as a basis for the testimony of the witness in respect of those portions of his 92 ter statement. Then I move on in relation to the same witness to P1181. The registrar is invited to replace the current content of P1181 with the set of documents contained in 65 ter number 2173. This is not a decision on admission of P1181. It's just that the content is now replaced and a decision on admission of P1181 will follow in writing. I now move on to Witness 28. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where I said I would move to Witness 28, I made a mistake, since I would first want to deliver a decision on the Prosecution's motion to admit evidence under Rule 92 quater. It is the Chamber's decision on the Prosecution's motion to admit evidence under Rule 92 quater, which was filed on the 5th of November, 2007. The Prosecution's motion concerns one of the witnesses who was added to the Prosecution's witness list following the Chamber's decision to amend the indictment, the Third Amended Indictment, on the 15th of October, 2007. On the 16th of October, 2007, the Prosecution sought to have the statement of this witness admitted pursuant to Rule 92 bis. When the presiding officer appointed by the Registrar attempted to obtain the necessary attestation, the witness refused. According to the Prosecution's motion, the witness stated on this occasion that he did not want to sign anything and that he would not go to The Hague unless he was forced to do so. The Prosecution has based its Rule 92 quater application on the witness's medical condition and the fact that the witness is of advanced age. The medical certificate accompanying the Prosecution's motion indicates that the witness suffers from physical and mental ailments, without further specifics, and that the witness has been under continuous medical treatments since 1999. The Defence for the three accused responded on the 8th, the 13th, and the 14th of November, 2007 that the Prosecution's motion should be denied.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'm loathe to interrupt. Has the Trial Chamber received the medical report which we filed today in which -- which was dated yesterday, which the doctor has specified in detail what the condition actually is?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I filed that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps that -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We filed that several hours ago. I don't think -- I'm told a courtesy copy wasn't distributed. That actually explains the witness's medical problem, which -- could I ask the Trial Chamber to visit that before -- respectfully, before --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll -- I'll interrupt --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the delivery of a decision. Nevertheless, Mr. Re, I -- you said, "I was told a courtesy copy wasn't distributed." That means that you require the Chamber to further consider its decision without even telling the Chamber at that time that new information was available which might have assisted us in organising our work.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Of course. But I'm -- I apologise. I didn't know you were about to deliver --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I didn't hear any apology until now.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, I'm just about to apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We -- I wasn't aware that the Trial Chamber hadn't received it. I can tell you in private session what the information is. I asked --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's read it during the first break.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it it was oversight?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Complete oversight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I thought it had been filed hours before. I'm just being told it was filed at 1.10. I thought it had been filed about four hours ago and provided to you. I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Insight sometimes works better than oversight. I'll move on and now deal with Witness 28. And I'd first like to deliver the Chamber's decision on the Prosecution's submission to admit into evidence a Human Rights Watch report through Witness 28. That is, therefore, a decision on admission of the Human Rights Watch report of October 1998 entitled "Humanitarian Law Violations in Kosovo." On the 12th of November, 2007, the Prosecution filed a motion requesting the admission of the entire report into evidence or, in the alternative, the admission of certain passages of the report. On the 15th, the 16th, and the 19th of November, 2007, the Defence for the three accused filed submissions opposing the admission of any parts of the report into evidence. As far as the report contains conclusions rather than provides facts, accepting this opinion evidence would encroach upon the Chamber's duty to draw inferences from facts. According to the Chamber, the following passages which the Prosecution found particularly relevant fall into the mentioned category: The opinion that the KLA committed serious violations of humanitarian law mentioned on the pages 3 to 7 of the report's summary; and on page 75 of Chapter 10, and the opinion stated in Chapter 11 of the report that by the end of February 1998, the conflict had reached a level of intensity sufficient to trigger the obligations of Common Article 3 of the Geneva Conventions. These parts are, in the Chamber's view, not suitable for admission. The Chamber also observes that many facts provided by the report are unsourced or are based on media reports or compilations of other human rights groups, thus consisting of multiple hearsay. Where there are references to eyewitnesses, they are often not named. Moreover, some of the factual information contained in the report merely repeats better evidence that already is before the Chamber. This is the case for the information relating to the conflict between the KLA and the Serb forces from January 1998 onwards --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This was French interpretation on the English Channel. I resume my last line. This is the case for the information relating to the conflict between the KLA and the Serb forces from January 1998 onwards, including the Serb attack on Likosane, contained in Chapter 3 of the report. This also applies to information about the disappearance of the persons named on pages 83 and 84 of Chapter 10 of the report. A large part of the report contains accounts of alleged crimes committed by Serb authorities against Kosovo Albanian civilians during 1998. The Chamber finds this repetitive to evidence that is already before the Chamber, may it be in a less detailed form. The relevance of this kind of information is such that there is no need for the Chamber to be provided with the detailed accounts of the report in order to be able to determine the matters before it. Chapter 10 of the report describes attacks against, and abductions of, ethnic Serbs, Roma, and Kosovo Albanians allegedly committed by the KLA. Lack of specificity and vagueness in relation to the gathering and processing of data underlying the overall numbers given prevent the Chamber from accepting this material for the purpose of drawing conclusions. This is the case in terms of the numbers of abducted Serbs provided by the report on page 75, as well as in terms of the numbers of attacked, injured, and killed Albanians provided by the Serbian Ministry of Internal Affairs cited by the report on page 75. As for the 14 incidents mentioned in this chapter where Serb, Roma, and Kosovar Albanians were attacked or abducted, many are not within the geographical scope of the indictment. For others, the report lacks information as to who the perpetrator was, or the information provided is a combination of multiple hearsay and lack of identified sources, so that it is of no assistance to the Chamber. As indicated before, for some of the incidents, the Chamber already has -- has better evidence, in the form of testimony of viva voce witnesses. For all the foregoing reasons, and pursuant to Rule 89(C), the Chamber denies admission into evidence of the Human Rights Watch report in its entirety. And this concludes the Chamber's decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm now moving to another set of exhibits in relation to Witness 28. Before doing so, Mr. Guy-Smith, has the Chamber interpreted the messages it received in relation to D195 through D202 correctly, if you do not press the admission of these documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then, Mr. Troop, I do understand that the Brahimaj Defence still presses admission of D203.

utterances.speaker: MR. TROOP
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that the position of the Brahimaj Defence in respect of D203 was further explained in -- in an e-mail sent by Mr. Harvey to one of the legal officers of the Chamber dated the 15th of November of 2007.

utterances.speaker: MR. TROOP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber has taken this into consideration. The Chamber has decided not to admit D203. But I would like to add one or two words to it. The Chamber is fully aware that the admission of D203 is a delicate and sensitive matter, because in that report the death of the mother and the grandmother of Mr. Brahimaj is described. Non-admission of D203 is totally unrelated to what the Chamber would be considered a -- an event which, of course, has had a huge impact on the son and the grandson of the deceased. It is exclusively on the basis of the procedural standards the Chamber has set that D203, which contains quite a lot of information, apart from the information I just described -- it's these procedural -- procedural standards which have led the Chamber to a decision to deny admission. The Chamber, at the same time, does not ignore what it means for someone to lose his mother and his grandmother. I then move on. I now move on to a decision on the admission into evidence of P1199, which was tendered through the witness Radomir Gojkovic. On the 31st of October, 2007, Exhibit P1199 was tendered as part of a series of exhibits relating to witness Radomir Gojkovic's 92 ter statement. The Defence pointed out that one of the documents contained in P1199 had already been tendered through Witness 69 and was subject to an objection by the Defence. The remainder of P1199 is comprised of two court-related documents: One being the authorisation of an investigation into alleged activities of Ramush Haradinaj and others by the District Court of Pec; and the other being a criminal police report to the Public Prosecutor of Pec relating to the investigation carried out by witness Radomir Gojkovic. The Defence has not objected to their admission. The Chamber considers these two documents to be both relevant and of probative value. The Chamber therefore decides to admit P1199 into evidence, apart from the document marked ERN U009-6873, which will be dealt with along with the other exhibits tendered through Witness 69. The Registrar is therefore instructed to remove the previously mentioned ERN number and the Chamber admits the remainder of P1199 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I move on and will deliver oral decisions on admission of a series of documents marked for identification D170 through D177. I first deal with D174, D175, and D177. These are witness statements given to the Prosecution. Such statements should be tendered through Rule 92 bis or 92 ter or 92 quater and cannot be admitted through witness Stijovic. The Chamber has decided not to admit D174, D175, and D177. D176 is a witness statement given to the Defence. It falls into the category I just mentioned since it is a statement taken for the purposes of the legal proceedings before this Tribunal. For those reasons, the Trial Chamber does not admit D176 into evidence. I now come to D170, D171, and D172. These documents, one being a report from the commander of the VJ 3rd Army to the VJ Supreme Command Staff; another one, a statement given by Radomir Markovic to the Serbian MUP; and a third to be a report from the Serbian MUP dealing with the so-called refrigerator truck case. Portions of these documents have been put to witness Stijovic, and therefore those portions are on the record. It has not been demonstrated that the remaining portions not put to the witnesses -- witness and therefore not yet on the record -- it has not been demonstrated that their relevance and probative value are of a level which would justify admission into evidence, and therefore D170, D171, and D172 are not admitted into evidence. I now come to D173. The Chamber admits D173 into evidence because the Chamber has considered that there are sufficiently relevant enough probative value so as to justify admission into evidence. I now move on to the documents marked for identification D220, D221, and D222. First of all, I would like to ask -- ask the registrar to replace the content of D222 with the content of document ID 2D001862, which is a complete version of the document the Defence intended to tender. I immediately add to that that the Chamber denies admission of D220 on the basis that -- let me just start my sentence again, because I may have given the impression that the replacement of D222 was followed by a decision of its admission. However, the decision on admission, at least this first decision on admission, deals with D220. The admission of D220 is denied. The transcript sufficiently reflects the relevant portions of D222 that were put to the witness; whereas, the remainder of the document does not qualify for admission. I now come to D221 and D222. The Chamber notes that there is no translation into English of these two documents. Mr. Guy-Smith, the Chamber asked itself whether it could still expect such a translation and/or whether you would press tendering D221 and D222, where the witness, I think, testified that he had not read these newspaper articles and where one could wonder whether there is dispute among the parties about the public attention the broadcasting the Balaj trial may have -- the attention the Balaj trial may have received at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I am in the process of having the article translated. Once translation is completed, which I believe will be by the end of today, I will reconsider my position. And with the Chamber's indulgence, will inform the Chamber tomorrow whether I will continue pressing the admission of these two exhibits based upon what the Chamber has just indicated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If that is not inconvenient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Then I understand --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber is --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I understand. I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- trying to get a clean desk as well. And therefore, Mr. Re, I'm approaching you. Would there be a great dispute about whether the -- the Dukagjini Trial of -- against Mr. Balaj would have received a lot of media attention at the time? Because that remains, as far as I understand, since the witness testified that he had not read.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: He was aware of the -- he was aware of the attention but had not read those particular articles. That is true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Apart from how relevant that exactly is that someone is aware that there's some media attention -- but, okay. Mr. Re, is there any dispute about wide -- a large media attention for the Balaj Dukagjini Trial at the time? It -- it's -- it appears a relatively marginal matter in the way it was introduced here.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I -- I just can't answer that. I don't know how much publicity the trial got in Kosovo, whether it was on the radio, TV, the papers -- I've got no idea. I can certainly make inquiries of people who were in Kosovo at the time. Maybe our field office could help us with the publicity given. But I -- I can't answer that standing here. I would have to make inquiries. I -- I do accept, of course, there was some publicity. Mr. Guy-Smith has -- has provided evidence of some publicity. But the extent of it is a different issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, now, Mr. -- Mr. Guy-Smith, apart from any other evidence that would -- that we would receive or have already received, what we see now is two newspaper articles, not full-page, relatively limited. Is there any possibility -- I mean, if you want us to draw inferences from this is part of a -- a huge media attention, which might well be the case but might not be the case -- these two newspaper articles as such do not say more than that they appeared and they paid attention to the trial. Mr. Re, would you -- would there be any dispute that at least two local newspapers published on the matter with publications covering, I would say, approximately one-eighth of a newspaper page, ordinary newspaper page, including -- and, Mr. Guy-Smith, help me out. Was there a photo on one or both of the newspaper articles of Mr. Balaj?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Of the articles thus far presented, there was a photo on -- on one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And there was his name in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, "Toger" and "Togeri" mentioned in relation to Balaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Right, on the other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- Mr. Re, in -- in the absence of any English translation, of course, we'll have difficulties to have it admitted into evidence. The facts I just mentioned, that is, in two newspaper articles -- in two newspapers articles were published of, if I could say, limited size - certainly not more than one/eighth of a newspaper article page - one of them including a photograph of Mr. Balaj, another one even without translation I could notice that close to where the word "Balaj" was used the word "Toger" or "Togeri" was used. Would that be in dispute?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The contents of those newspapers, the publication --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I set it out now.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No, that's not in dispute. But I can't take it any further at this second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Guy-Smith, to have these two documents in evidence -- and it's not disputed that it relates to the -- to the trial, Mr. Re. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I -- I'm accepting Mr. Guy-Smith's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- undertaking --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- representation that it does.

utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I do not believe that the translation of the article itself will give any further information which will be particularly of help to the Chamber's analysis. I -- I do believe, obviously - and I think the Chamber knows precisely why I'm interested in one having in the record a photograph that shows my client displayed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that's not in dispute any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: My only concern is whether or not there's -- at some point in time somebody is -- may need to refer to those two facts. By that I mean looking at a picture or seeing the two names together. And it may be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If in future someone may testify that he has read this, or whatever, then, of course, vacating at this moment D203 is not a decision which would be valid for eternity.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If it's not valid for eternity, then I'm satisfied. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That means that -- Let me just confer with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber has decided that D203 will be vacated and that apart from the context in which such an application would be made, by that -- as such vacating D203, has no prejudicial effect on any future application -- I don't know. You never know what happens. Of course, not this week, not by the Prosecution but -- because the Prosecution is supposed not to -- at this moment to introduce through a motion any further evidence. But therefore D203 is now vacated.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could I -- could I just rise very briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just to check that the Trial Chamber intended to refer to D203.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm making a mistake, as a matter of fact, because we are talking about D221 and D222. So what I just said about D203 actually refers to the two newspaper articles, which we find under D221 and D222. Therefore, Mr. Registrar --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- D203 was already -- the status was changed already to "not admitted," and the vacation should be in relation to D221 and D222. I apologise for the mistake. The next matter I would like to raise -- yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then finally, the Chamber will have to decide on the Prosecution's application to hear the testimony of Witness 30 by videolink. Today the Chamber received a response to that motion filed by the Haradinaj Defence. I am not aware at this moment whether any --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: We joined.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You joined. Mr. Troop.

utterances.speaker: MR. TROOP
utterances.text: Yes, a joinder was filed on behalf of the Brahimaj team as well prior to 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If it is of any assistance, it was at approximately 11.13 this morning. 11.19.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I meanwhile have seen the -- I had seen already the Haradinaj response. I have now in front of me Idriz Balaj joinder. I have not yet in front of me -- oh, yes, Brahimaj. I also see that. Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I'm -- I'm specifically looking at the joinder filings to see whether anything is added to the Haradinaj filing, and I see that --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If it's of any help, we added nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You didn't add anything at all. Why was this important? Because if there would be -- have been added anything, the Chamber might have found this a reason to reconsider a decision which we prepared on the basis of -- on the basis of the filing by the Haradinaj Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber will deliver a decision today but will not do that before the break. Then, Mr. Registrar, is there already any information about the availability of the witness on the location of the videolink?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In order to further prepare for the videolink, we'll have a break a bit longer than we usually have, and we'll resume at quarter past 4.00

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume the hearing in the case against Haradinaj and others. The first thing I'd like to do is to establish whether the videolink is functioning. Can you hear me and can you see me at the location?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Yes, Your Honour, we can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. And I suggest that everyone present in the room of the videolink introduces himself. I -- I think as the representative of the Registry we recognise on our screen Evelyn Anoya. Could you invite the other persons to introduce themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. DAVIDSON
utterances.text: [Via videolink] My name is Paul Davidson. I work for the Federal Public Defenders office in the Federal Court in the Southern District of New York in the United States. utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That is clear. You may be aware that in view of -- no, but let me first continue and ask all the others to introduce themselves. Mr. Davidson, right to you is sitting?

utterances.speaker: MR. TARLOW
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Thank you, Judge. It's Richard Tarlow, Assistant United States attorney for the Southern District of New York and I represent the United States of America.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tarlow. And in the middle, you are Mr. Kabashi?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it's me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, interpreters, are there any interpreters present at the location of the videolink?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the services of CLSS in The Hague are used. Perhaps it would be good to clearly explain to Mr. Kabashi in what procedural situation we find ourselves at this moment. And that is we are in a court hearing which is part of the trial against three accused: Mr. Haradinaj, Mr. Balaj, and Mr. Brahimaj. And I'd like, just for your information, I'd like Mr. Kabashi, that you are aware of who are in this courtroom. The Prosecution is represented by Mr. Re. I don't know whether you can see him at this moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then as lead counsel of Mr. Haradinaj, Mr. Emmerson is present. As lead counsel for Mr. Balaj, Mr. Guy-Smith is present. And as counsel for Mr. Brahimaj, Mr. Troop is present. It is important for you to know, Mr. Kabashi, that although you have been indicted for contempt in this Tribunal, that at this moment we are not hearing your contempt case, but we, the Chamber, would like to hear the evidence you would give in the case against the accused in The Hague. And before you give evidence, you are required to make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Could the representative of the Registry hand out to Mr. Kabashi the text of the solemn declaration and --

utterances.speaker: MR. DAVIDSON
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honour, I should perhaps short circuit this by clarifying that -- that Mr. Kabashi is not prepared to testify today and -- and does not intend to give evidence in this proceeding today. utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Kabashi, are you -- where I asked you to make a solemn declaration, are you refusing to make a solemn declaration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I'm not refusing. I don't need to give a solemn declaration, because I am not here to testify. That's the reason why my counsel will represent me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Kabashi, unfortunately your counsel cannot replace you as a witness. Therefore, I invite you to make the solemn declaration, because only after the solemn declaration has been given by you, questions can be put by us. And we then will find out whether or not you are failing or refusing to answer questions. So therefore, I invite you again to make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. DAVIDSON
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Once again, Mr. Kabashi has decided, after consultation with counsel, not to give evidence today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'd like to hear that from Mr. Kabashi, rather than from counsel, because he is not represented. He is a witness. And although you may represent him in any concept proceedings, representation of a witness is not something known before this Tribunal. Of course, representation of accused persons is something well-known here. That means that counsel speak for an accused. However, Mr. Kabashi at this moment does not appear as an accused but appears as someone who has been called to testify as a witness. So therefore, if Mr. Kabashi doesn't want to testify, we'd like to hear from him. And the first step is that invited to make a solemn declaration, that we'll observe what he does. Does he make that solemn declaration? If he does not make that solemn declaration, we'll see. Mr. Kabashi, you are invited for the third time now by me to make the solemn declaration. And, Mr. Kabashi, if you don't want to do that, please tell me.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] One moment, Your Honour. We're just hearing the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Mr. -- Mr. Kabashi, I invited you to make a solemn declaration. Would you please make that solemn declaration, the text of which Ms. Anoya will be handed out to the witness. Or if you don't have it available, I'll speak the words and ask Mr. Kabashi to repeat them.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] If you could assist, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Kabashi, I invite you to repeat the following words: "I solemnly declare."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "That I will speak the truth."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That I will speak the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "The whole truth, and nothing but the truth."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated, Mr. Kabashi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kabashi, I now give an opportunity to Mr. Re, who is counsel for the Prosecution, to examine you. Mr. Re, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Kabashi. Is your name Shefqet Kabashi and were you born on the 1st of July, 1976 in Zahac in Peja, in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kabashi, would you please answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I just answered that. I said "yes."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, that was not translated.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It was not heard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was not heard and not translated. Please proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And are you an ethnic Kosovar Albanian and a Muslim by religion?

utterances.speaker: SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I am Albanian, an ethnic Albanian, and without any religion. And as Albanian that I am, I have told you that you are destroying the lives of people in my country.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you please -- would you please answer the questions and refrain from commenting on anything else. Please proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And your -- your occupation -- your occupation. Did you work for the KPS in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: [In English] I'm sorry. [Interpretation] I am not in a position to testify to such a Tribunal. I am not prepared to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Mr. -- Mr. Kabashi -- Mr. Kabashi, I want to ask you some questions. I'm not going to ask you anything about the contempt proceedings. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I am not prepared to speak before this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Kabashi, I'm not going to ask you anything about the contempt proceedings. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Irrespective of what you are going to ask me, I know that you are the one who has indicted me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No, it's the Trial Chamber which has indicted you, not me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kabashi. Mr. Kabashi, it was the Trial Chamber that issued the order of an indictment, and it was not the Office of the Prosecution. Mr. Kabashi, a question was put to you which was the following question. The question was: Did you work for the KPS in Kosovo? You have not answered that question. Do you refuse to answer that question?

utterances.speaker: SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I said that from what I know of your legislation, I know that the Prosecutor has indicted me and that the Trial Chamber has accepted that. With respect to questions -- to the questions you are putting me, it's not that I don't want to answer them but I am not in a position to speak before you. I want my counsel to -- to represent me. I cannot really speak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kabashi, I again put to you the question that was formulated by Mr. Re, that is, whether you worked for the KPS in Kosovo. And I urge you to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DAVIDSON
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honour, this is Paul Davidson, once again. With all respect, Mr. Kabashi has indicated that he's not prepared to testify today. And I think he will persist in that decision here this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then if Mr. Kabashi tells me that he does not answer the question that was just put to him and he will not answer any other question, then we might finish soon. Yes, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honour, there may -- there may well be a solution here. I'm not sure that Mr. Davidson, with -- with due respect to him and his position, is fully aware of the proceedings or the procedure here. It could well be, if you allow us a short adjournment in the presence of Mr. Karnavas to speak to Mr. Davidson. Mr. Di Fazio had a brief conversation with him before. utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There is a suggestion made by Mr. Re. Any objection by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I -- I'm assuming that the invitation is extended to Defence counsel? To be present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To be present? During?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Any discussions that take place at this stage between representatives of the witness and representatives of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. I was going to ask the same question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, the issue might be that the witness, once already started to give testimony, although not for a very long time, and therefore the question is to what extent you're free to speak with the witness and counsel any more. utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, I'm -- procedurally I'm unclear about a couple of things, so I'm not sure how -- how to respond to the answering of that question. utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber has considered it. Mr. Re, the Chamber can imagine two different scenarios. The one is that Mr. Kabashi speaks with Mr. Karnavas and you in the presence of the Defence counsel, or that Mr. Karnavas and Mr. Davidson speak with Mr. Kabashi and further advise him on his present situation. If I am misinformed, I'd like to know at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I take it, Mr. Re, that Mr. Karnavas specifically for those purposes is assigned in order to complement the -- the knowledge and the skills of Mr. Davidson.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: My -- I am anxious to ensure that the interests of justice are served and Mr. -- Mr. Kabashi testifies and provides the valuable evidence which should be heard by the Tribunal. The Defence are very anxious that Mr. Kabashi doesn't testify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I wish to speak to Mr. Davidson in Mr. Karnavas' presence to explain the procedures to Mr. Davidson. I would also explain to him how two people were indicted for contempt last week and the charges of the contempt were withdrawn --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- after the person testified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. That is --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That is relevant information --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I think what Mr. Re is doing right now is, quite frankly, improper. I want to say two things. Earlier on Mr. Re used the word "farce" or the phrase "descending into a farce," which I take umbrage to. Second of all, what Mr. Re just said, I take umbrage to. I don't have -- as we would say in the United States, I don't have a dog in this fight. As friend to the court, as a friend to any court, whether I am practicing here in The Hague or I am practicing back home in the United States, I think it's important that any individual, whoever is in a position where they have potential legal problems, especially where they've been indicted, has the independent and considered advice of counsel. And that is my interest as an officer of the court, no more, no less.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How could his interests be served by a lawyer in the States who is does not understand the procedures --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- and we haven't spoken to him to explain them to him?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, you earlier did send messages over the videolink, messages of which -- which should not be sent at this moment by a party who is not in a position any more to directly communicate with the witness.
